message.reasoning:
I'm catching a units error with the avogadro factor being double-counted—K0 already includes NA per gram, so Berger's formula uses K0·ZA directly in MeV cm²/g, meaning I need to compute the electron density per cm properly instead of reapplying NA.

So σ per electron becomes K0·ZA/(β²T)·∫F dx, which means my code should multiply K0 by ZA (0.55509) directly rather than also multiplying by the NEW factor—that was the bug causing the double normalization. The CDF-based sampling fraction is unaffected by this normalization since it's already relative, so that part is fine as is.

Plugging numbers in: K0 comes out to roughly 0.1536 MeV·cm²/mol, scaled by 0.555/0.889 gives about 0.096, and multiplying by the integral of 1/x² over the relevant x range (~100) lands me around 9.6 deltas/cm, which lines up reasonably well with the ~8.5 figure I had earlier.
